papers.title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
papers.abstract: A minimal realisation of warm inflation, even within the Standard Model, assumes that the inflaton $φ$ couples via the effective operator $φ\, G\tilde G$. We show that the SM solutions are in tension with the plasma calculation (as each sphaleron transition releases an energy much larger than the temperature) and with the assumed effective operator description. papers.title: SciCheck: A Framework for Verifying the Integrity of Deep Learning Training
papers.abstract: Deep learning training is difficult to verify within a scientific workflow: its architecture, hyperparameters, and procedure are rarely fixed until training has been attempted, and two honest runs never produce the same weights, so recomputation cannot serve as a check. papers.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
papers.abstract: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. papers.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
papers.abstract: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. papers.title: Scenario Orchestration for Closed-loop Policy Evaluation of Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Scenario-based simulation is central to evaluating autonomous-driving policies, but a scenario scripted before execution (i.e., with predetermined, fixed actor routes and speeds) may not preserve its intended interaction once the tested ego policy responds in closed loop. papers.title: FlowMoP: Stochastic Multi-Person Motion Prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting the future motion of multiple people is inherently stochastic: the same observed history admits many plausible continuations depending on intent, coordination, and social context.
